check.reason: The item misstates the story. The real headline is about a simple UTI that turns into a $1,756 bill. The take invents a different scenario: an urgent care visit retroactively billed as an emergency department visit, over a 'cough'. Nothing in the headline or summary says this happened, and the cough is unrelated to a UTI. This presents an invented fact about the case as if it were the story. The target (billing) is acceptable and patients aren't mocked, but the premise needs to be rewritten around what the story reports, such as how a routine UTI visit becomes a $1,756 bill, without made-up details like the urgent-care-to-ER upgrade or the cough.

pick.title: How a simple UTI turns into a $1,756 bill
pick.headline: Urgent Care Visit Upgraded to Emergency Room, Retroactively, on Invoice Only
pick.take: The sign out front said urgent care. The claim said emergency department. Nothing about the cough changed, but billing has a gift for promoting a visit after the patient has gone home. Patients can't verify which description will be honored, and the one with a dollar amount attached usually wins.
